ingredients.item: butterflied lamb shoulder , trimmed of thick fat caps but left with a thin fat layer
ingredients.preparation: or leg steaks cut 2 cm thick

ingredients.item: /2 Asian pear , grated and squeezed nearly dry
Steamed rice , perilla and lettuce ssam, ssamjang , kkaennip jangajji pickled perilla or quick-pickled onion, kimchi

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Slice the marinated shoulder across the grain into strips 2 cm wide. Sear in a single layer on the medium-hot zone — lamb's fat wants to flare, so the grill boss stays at the grate with tongs, moving strips to the cool corner when their edges catch.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the strips should sear to a deep brown-red crust with light char at the fat edges, and the smell should be the pastes toasting over rendered lamb fat — rich enough that the table will ask what it is before it is ready.

instructions.heading: Work in batches, brush as each batch finishes
instructions.action: Work in batches, brush as each batch finishes: 2–3 minutes a side for medium-rare to medium (lamb's just-pink center at 57–60 °C is where the juiciness lives; well-done lamb shoulder is a lost cause at any heat), a stroke of the reserved marinade on the hot slices as they come off.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: a test strip cut at the grill station: crust, then just-pink juicy center, and the pastes' savory-heat arriving behind the lamb's big flavor rather than on top of it. If the marinade reads louder than the meat, the strips were thin or the marinade thick — the meat is the headline at this table.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Rest the batches 3 minutes on a warm platter as they come off, sesame over, and the platter goes to the table's center for ssam service: perilla leaf, a swipe of ssamjang (#SA01), a hot strip, a piece of pickled perilla or onion, fold, one bite.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the ssam test: the perilla's anise edge against the lamb's richness with the pickled cut through the fat is the record's finished thought — rich, sharp, herbal, one bite. If the wrap collapses into pure richness, the pickle was skipped; it is load-bearing here.

storageNotes: Marinated shoulder keeps 24 hours, freezes 1 month. Cooked, 3 days — leftover slices into a gimbap-style roll or a rice bowl with the last reserved marinade warmed as sauce.

Variations: the same marinade on lamb chops (shorter marinate, 4 hours); beef short rib takes this paste beautifully for a nontraditional weeknight galbi (#M03's cut, this record's flavor); mushroom caps in the reserved marinade grill alongside for the table's vegetarians.
